holidays.name: National Public Sleeping Day
holidays.description: A day that gives you permission to snooze in public. Nap on a park bench, doze on a train, or curl up in a quiet corner of the library. Just don't expect everyone to cooperate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is often linked to the idea that rest deserves a place in everyday life, not only in the bedroom.
holidays.funFact: Many cultures treat public napping as normal. In Japan, the practice of 'inemuri' means dozing off in public, and it is often read as a sign of hard work.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Soufflé Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the dessert that is airy, rich and a little dramatic. Chocolate soufflés are famous for rising high in the oven and, if you aren't careful, collapsing just as fast. Today is a good excuse to bake one or order one.
holidays.origin: The soufflé comes from France and first appeared in cookbooks in the early 18th century. This chocolate-themed day is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: The word soufflé comes from the French verb 'souffler', meaning 'to blow' or 'to puff up'.

holidays.name: National Tooth Fairy Day
holidays.description: A day for the tiny, coin-leaving visitor who trades cash for baby teeth. Celebrate by sharing tooth-loss stories, writing a note to the Tooth Fairy, or helping a child with a wobbly tooth.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is part of a long tradition of customs around children's lost teeth.
holidays.funFact: In Spanish-speaking countries, the tooth-collecting figure is often a mouse called Ratoncito Pérez, not a fairy.
